Incoming Students Erasmus+ Incoming Students International Welcome Day – A.Y. 2025/2026 II semester The International Welcome Day for incoming students arriving the second semester will take place on the 23rd February from 9.30 to 13.00 at Great Hall in Via Ostiense 133 (Aula Magna Rettorato). It is necessary for students to follow the instructions sent by the International Mobility Office via e-mail in order to be enrolled. What to do before coming to Roma Tre (Application Form) If you are going to spend your Erasmus study period at Roma Tre: ensure that your University communicated your nomination by e-mail to the International Mobility Office (incoming.students@uniroma3.it) . fill in the Application Form . The application form must be printed, signed by the student and by the sending institution. Then it must be uploaded through the temporary link that you will receive by e-mail after submitting the application. You will receive confirmation of acceptance by e-mail. Application form deadlines: from 30th March to 15th June for students arriving in the first semester or for the entire academic year from 30th September to 15th November for students arriving in the second semester Roma Tre offers free Italian language courses for Erasmus students. To attend the Italian language courses, you must enrol in advance through the website of Centro Linguistico di Ateneo. It is necessary to make sure you have a valid health insurance in Italy (before leaving, check that there is an agreement with the Italian state). Enrolment at Roma Tre University To be enrolled as Erasmus student , it is necessary to take part to the Erasmus Welcome Day or send a ticket through https://help.uniroma3.it/ uploading a copy of the following compulsory documents (please in only one attachment): proof of your arrival in Rome (flight ticket and boarding pass, train or bus ticket, etc); copy of Identity card/passport. Erasmus incoming students will be provided with a certificate attesting their enrolment at Roma Tre as Erasmus student and credentials (User Id and password) to access their Reserved Area of Student Portal. Through the Student Portal students will be able to check their academic career, enroll for exams and print certificates such as the Transcript of Records. Study Plan and Learning Agreement Erasmus incoming students must contact their Erasmus departmental Coordinator immediately after their enrollment to define a study plan, to sign a Learning Agreement, to get information about courses , courses in English and teachers. Our Office and the Erasmus Institutional Coordinator are at disposal to support and guide incoming students in their initial phase of stay and throughout the Erasmus period. Our Erasmus Institutional Coordinator is available to receive students by appointment. Any changes to the study plan entered in the Application Form must be done also in the Student Personal Page (log in with the same User Id and a password received by e-mail). By 30th October for students arriving in the first semester and by 31st March for students arriving in the second semester, the Learning Agreement completed with all signatures must be uploaded on the Personal Page. A copy of the Learning Agreement must be provided via Personal Page, otherwise the certificate of stay can’t be issued. ECTS grading Tables Certificate of Attendance In order to receive the attendance certificate, the student has to upload proof of departure from Rome (flight ticket and boarding pass are both necessary, or train ticket, bus ticket, etc) on the Student Personal Page . International Mobility » Erasmus+ Incoming Students Erasmus+ Incoming Students International Welcome Day – A.Y. 2025/2026 II semester The International Welcome Day for incoming students arriving the second semester will take place on the 23rd February from 9.30 to 13.00 at Great Hall in Via Ostiense 133 (Aula Magna Rettorato). It is necessary for students to follow the instructions sent by the International Mobility Office via e-mail in order to be enrolled. What to do before coming to Roma Tre (Application Form) If you are going to spend your Erasmus study period at Roma Tre: ensure that your University communicated your nomination by e-mail to the International Mobility Office (incoming.students@uniroma3.it) . fill in the Application Form . The application form must be printed, signed by the student and by the sending institution. Then it must be uploaded through the temporary link that you will receive by e-mail after submitting the application. You will receive confirmation of acceptance by e-mail. Application form deadlines: from 30th March to 15th June for students arriving in the first semester or for the entire academic year from 30th September to 15th November for students arriving in the second semester Roma Tre offers free Italian language courses for Erasmus students. To attend the Italian language courses, you must enrol in advance through the website of Centro Linguistico di Ateneo. It is necessary to make sure you have a valid health insurance in Italy (before leaving, check that there is an agreement with the Italian state). Enrolment at Roma Tre University To be enrolled as Erasmus student , it is necessary to take part to the Erasmus Welcome Day or send a ticket through https://help.uniroma3.it/ uploading a copy of the following compulsory documents (please in only one attachment): proof of your arrival in Rome (flight ticket and boarding pass, train or bus ticket, etc); copy of Identity card/passport. Erasmus incoming students will be provided with a certificate attesting their enrolment at Roma Tre as Erasmus student and credentials (User Id and password) to access their Reserved Area of Student Portal. Through the Student Portal students will be able to check their academic career, enroll for exams and print certificates such as the Transcript of Records. Study Plan and Learning Agreement Erasmus incoming students must contact their Erasmus departmental Coordinator immediately after their enrollment to define a study plan, to sign a Learning Agreement, to get information about courses , courses in English and teachers. Our Office and the Erasmus Institutional Coordinator are at disposal to support and guide incoming students in their initial phase of stay and throughout the Erasmus period. Our Erasmus Institutional Coordinator is available to receive students by appointment. Any changes to the study plan entered in the Application Form must be done also in the Student Personal Page (log in with the same User Id and a password received by e-mail). By 30th October for students arriving in the first semester and by 31st March for students arriving in the second semester, the Learning Agreement completed with all signatures must be uploaded on the Personal Page. A copy of the Learning Agreement must be provided via Personal Page, otherwise the certificate of stay can’t be issued. ECTS grading Tables Certificate of Attendance In order to receive the attendance certificate, the student has to upload proof of departure from Rome (flight ticket and boarding pass are both necessary, or train ticket, bus ticket, etc) on the Student Personal Page . Home » International » Study at Roma Tre » Whom to contact Whom to contact It is our great pleasure to extend a very warm welcome to everyone! We hope this web site will meet your information needs and, for those unfamiliar with the University, provide a comprehensive introduction to our work, to our aspirations and achievements and to the many opportunities we offer for partnership and participation in the pursuit of our goals. There are a number of factors that make this a particularly exciting and dynamic period in the history of the University among which the increasing recognition of the high quality of our teaching and research, the continuous development of the capital city of which we have the privilege to be part, a number of ambitious and visionary projects. Through the efforts of a dedicated and talented staff, the University has established itself as a progressive and successful centre of higher education and earned its current position among the front rank of Italian universities. Our success serves further to fuel our ambition as we increase our service to society – locally, nationally and internationally. Our main mission is to produce knowledge and to transfer it within an international horizon. We want to provide our students with the necessary skills for a quick and satisfactory entrance into the labour market. Our motto is ‘learning by doing‘. Whether you are a prospective student or a current student; a staff member or collaborator; or one of our many other stakeholders, we hope you benefit from your visit to this site and any further interaction with the University. Home » International » Study at Roma Tre » Whom to contact Whom to contact It is our great pleasure to extend a very warm welcome to everyone! We hope this web site will meet your information needs and, for those unfamiliar with the University, provide a comprehensive introduction to our work, to our aspirations and achievements and to the many opportunities we offer for partnership and participation in the pursuit of our goals. There are a number of factors that make this a particularly exciting and dynamic period in the history of the University among which the increasing recognition of the high quality of our teaching and research, the continuous development of the capital city of which we have the privilege to be part, a number of ambitious and visionary projects. Through the efforts of a dedicated and talented staff, the University has established itself as a progressive and successful centre of higher education and earned its current position among the front rank of Italian universities. Our success serves further to fuel our ambition as we increase our service to society – locally, nationally and internationally. Our main mission is to produce knowledge and to transfer it within an international horizon. We want to provide our students with the necessary skills for a quick and satisfactory entrance into the labour market. Our motto is ‘learning by doing‘. Whether you are a prospective student or a current student; a staff member or collaborator; or one of our many other stakeholders, we hope you benefit from your visit to this site and any further interaction with the University. and Services Information and Services In this section you can find useful information and services supplied by University Roma Tre to incoming students (Erasmus, Exchange, Marco Polo). Registration with the Anagrafe for EU students Students coming from the European Union who will stay in Italy for a period of more than 3 months must register at the Town Hall of residence (Iscrizione Anagrafica) . Non-EU Students applying for visas: Non-EU students living abroad who need to apply for a study visa should contact the Italian Consulates. Visa for Italy Universitaly Residence Permit for non-EU students Non-EU students, who plan to stay in Italy for more than 3 months, must request a Residence Permit within 8 working days of arrival in Italy. After enrolment at Roma Tre, they must go to a post office with the desk “ Sportello Amico ” to apply for residence permit. For any other information about residence permit, call: 848.855.888 for information about the status of application (Monday to Friday, from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.) or visit the website of Ministero dell’Interno for general information. Non-EU students have to show proof of certified health insurance coverage in Italy (it is recommended to have a copy certified by the Italian Consulate or by Embassy in your own country). Otherwise, foreign students may buy a private insurance policy in Italy. Tax code To open a bank account or apply for a canteen card, it is necessary to have a tax code. It is possible to apply for it at the Agenzia delle Entrate located in Via Ippolito Nievo, 48-50, tel: 06.58.31.91 e-mail: dp.iroma@agenziaentrate.it (metro B stop “Piramide”, then tram n.3 stop Piazza Ippolito Nievo). Individuals – Tax identification number for foreign citizens – Agenzia delle Entrate (agenziaentrate.gov.it) University canteens University canteens provide low cost meals . They are managed by Link identifier #identifier__90222-6 DiSCo Lazio (Ente Regionale per il Diritto allo Studio e alla Conoscenza) . Academic information Departments of Roma Tre Roma Tre Course Catalogue Academic calendar: 1st October – start of teaching activities and first cycle of lessons for 10/13 weeks January/February – 4/6 weeks examinations of the reference academic year 1st March – start of the second cycle of lessons for 10/13 weeks June/July – 4/6 weeks exams 1-30 September – tests of the reference academic year For the timetable of the lessons and the dates of the exams you can contact the Departments. and Services Information and Services In this section you can find useful information and services supplied by University Roma Tre to incoming students (Erasmus, Exchange, Marco Polo). Registration with the Anagrafe for EU students Students coming from the European Union who will stay in Italy for a period of more than 3 months must register at the Town Hall of residence (Iscrizione Anagrafica) . Non-EU Students applying for visas: Non-EU students living abroad who need to apply for a study visa should contact the Italian Consulates. Visa for Italy Universitaly Residence Permit for non-EU students Non-EU students, who plan to stay in Italy for more than 3 months, must request a Residence Permit within 8 working days of arrival in Italy. After enrolment at Roma Tre, they must go to a post office with the desk “ Sportello Amico ” to apply for residence permit. For any other information about residence permit, call: 848.855.888 for information about the status of application (Monday to Friday, from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.) or visit the website of Ministero dell’Interno for general information. Non-EU students have to show proof of certified health insurance coverage in Italy (it is recommended to have a copy certified by the Italian Consulate or by Embassy in your own country). Otherwise, foreign students may buy a private insurance policy in Italy. Tax code To open a bank account or apply for a canteen card, it is necessary to have a tax code. It is possible to apply for it at the Agenzia delle Entrate located in Via Ippolito Nievo, 48-50, tel: 06.58.31.91 e-mail: dp.iroma@agenziaentrate.it (metro B stop “Piramide”, then tram n.3 stop Piazza Ippolito Nievo). Individuals – Tax identification number for foreign citizens – Agenzia delle Entrate (agenziaentrate.gov.it) University canteens University canteens provide low cost meals . They are managed by Link identifier #identifier__90222-6 DiSCo Lazio (Ente Regionale per il Diritto allo Studio e alla Conoscenza) .
